title: Signal Garden — Bioluminescent Ecosystem Synth

checks.name: headless simulation and UI self-test
checks.details: 19/19 passed. Runs the real inline script from index.html in a Node vm against a Canvas2D/DOM stub. Verifies: boots populated with no user input; three distinct organism classes; render issues fills/strokes/gradients and composites the trail and glow layers; seed 4242 reproduces byte-identical initial state while a different seed does not; fixed timestep advances ~1.0s of sim in both 60 frames at 60fps and 20 frames at 20fps; 4 simulated minutes without collapse or runaway; energy/population/clock readouts update and match the world; presets 1-3 switch; P/R/Space/1-3 keys; click plants a beacon, drag paints nutrient, pointer motion bends drifters; pulses excite blooms; bloom->drifter and hunter->drifter energy transfer; births and deaths both occur; depleted blooms go dormant and recover; resize preserves and rescales the world; audio starts muted and toggles; accessible description is populated; no non-finite values after heavy interaction.

checks.name: self-test under prefers-reduced-motion
checks.details: 19/19 passed with the reduced-motion code path active (smaller population, shorter trails, fewer particles, softer bloom pass). Confirms the reduced experience is still a complete, running ecosystem rather than a degraded one.

checks.name: long-run ecosystem balance probe
checks.details: All three presets pass over 4 simulated minutes each. Measured 110.8 / 106.8 / 76.5 bloom openings per minute, live signal waves during 99% / 97% / 100% of ticks, and drifter populations never dropping below 46 / 52 / 33 (the emergency floor is 8). Thresholds require >=30 openings/min, >=75% signal liveness, and bounded populations, so this asserts the attract state stays visually interesting indefinitely, not merely alive.

checks.name: balance probe under prefers-reduced-motion
checks.details: All three presets pass against thresholds scaled to the intentionally smaller, calmer reduced-motion world: 26.3 / 45.0 / 39.3 openings per minute, signals live 89% / 91% / 99% of ticks, drifters never below 31 / 28 / 26.

checks.name: real-browser smoke test in headless Chrome over file://
checks.details: 22/22 passed loading the page from file:// in headless Chrome. Verifies what a Node stub cannot: real 2D context at 1600x813; 92% of sampled canvas pixels non-black after a forced paint; ctx.filter blur available; real KeyboardEvent dispatch for P, R, Space (including cooldown) and 1/2/3; real PointerEvent click, drag and touch-type pointers; all 7 buttons keyboard-focusable and in the tab order; audio muted by default with Web Audio present; canvas exposed as role=img with aria-describedby and a substantive live description; zero remote references in the served DOM; resize does not reset the ecosystem; and no uncaught errors or console errors during boot, interaction, and a live render run.

checks.name: frame cost measurement
checks.details: 18.1 ms per full sim+render frame at 1600x813 with Skia forced to flush each frame, measured under headless Chrome with --disable-gpu, i.e. pure CPU rasterisation, which is several times slower than the GPU-backed canvas a real viewer gets. The simulation step alone is 0.100 ms, so rendering dominates and the physics never gates the frame. Profiling during development cut this from 45.7 ms by moving the bloom blur to half resolution, replacing 'high' with bilinear resampling for the nutrient upscale, rendering the two soft haze layers into the half-res buffer, drawing bloom and relay wavefronts only in that buffer, and stroking each corolla in a single path.

checks.name: no remote runtime references
checks.details: No matches. index.html is a single self-contained file (68 KB) with one inline <script>, inline CSS, no src/href/@import/url() references, no fetch/XHR/WebSocket, no fonts, images, or CDN links. The browser check independently confirms zero remote references in the live DOM.

checks.name: visual verification of all three presets and reduced motion
checks.details: Captured and visually inspected the default 1600x900 frame for each preset plus a --force-prefers-reduced-motion run. Each preset is distinctly styled (Abyssal Bloom: teal/green blooms, cyan drifters, coral hunters; Ultraviolet Shoal: violet blooms, cyan shoal, lime hunters; Ember Reef: lime/gold blooms, amber drifters, crimson hunters), the water reads deep and near-black, the three organism silhouettes are separable at a glance, and signal waves, trails, and energy rings are all legible rather than particle noise. The reduced-motion frame shows the expected smaller population and short trails while remaining the same experience.

summary: A self-contained Canvas 2D artwork in a single 68 KB index.html that opens directly from disk with no build, server, or network. A deterministic seeded ecosystem runs on a fixed 1/60 s timestep: anchored blooms absorb nutrient light and burst open, mobile drifters ferry that energy between them leaving fading bioluminescent wakes, and rare hunters stalk the most energised drifters and emit disruption waves that briefly silence local signals. Energy transfer, birth, reproduction, dormancy, and death are all readable from the visuals, and signal pulses propagate organism to organism through spatial-hash neighbour queries rather than all-to-all comparisons. Pointer motion bends trails like a current, click plants a signal beacon, drag paints a nutrient current, Space fires a global pulse on a visible cooldown, P pauses, R walks the deterministic seed sequence, and 1/2/3 switch three curated presets. A compact HUD reports population, energy, seed, elapsed sim time, and the active preset. Audio is opt-in and off by default with no blocking modal; prefers-reduced-motion trims population, trail persistence, and flashes while keeping the ecosystem intact; the canvas carries a live accessible description and every control is keyboard-reachable with a visible focus ring.
known_issues: Frame cost was measured only under headless Chrome with --disable-gpu (18.1 ms/frame at 1600x813, pure CPU rasterisation). Headless Chrome on this machine hung when GPU rasterisation was enabled, so the faster GPU-backed number a real viewer sees could not be measured directly; the recorded figure is the worst-case software path.
The browser check requires a local Chrome or Chromium and exits with status 2 if none is found. The artwork itself has no such dependency.

Audio is a small optional layer (pentatonic plucks on bloom openings, drifter division, and hunter strikes). It is off by default and the piece is designed to be complete when muted, so it received far less tuning than the visuals.
